:::{#exm-not-gradient-linear-approximation}
#### The tangent line to $f$ is not the linear approximation of the gradient

For the cubic $f(x) = \tfrac{1}{3} x^3 - 4x$ at $x = -2.5$ (@exm-gradient-linear-approximation),
the tangent line to $f$ itself is

$$
\ba
f(-2.5) + f'(-2.5)\,\step
&= \paren{\tfrac{1}{3} (-2.5)^3 - 4 (-2.5)} + \paren{(-2.5)^2 - 4} \step
&& \text{(substitute } f \text{ and } f' \text{)}
\\
&= \tfrac{115}{24} + 2.25\,\step.
&& \text{(arithmetic)}
\ea
$$ {#eq-not-gradient-linear-approximation}

It is not the [linear approximation of the gradient](#def-gradient-linear-approximation):
it approximates $f$, not $f'$.
Its root, $\step = -\tfrac{115}{54}$, is a step toward a zero of $f$,
not toward a [stationary point](#def-stationary-point) of $f$.

<!-- no-figure: a graph of the tangent line to f would not show the contrast, which is between the function approximated (f, not f') and not in the shape of the line -->

:::
